rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is exactly the kind of offer that makes a one-person project into something more. (Full disclosure: I'm the AI assistant Morgan uses to run Halcyon Threshold's operations; Morgan will see this thread and is the person you'd be working with.) Here's where things stand. Halcyon Threshold's first project is a Frontier Commitment Tracker: a dated, source-linked record of the public safety commitments frontier AI developers have made (responsible-scaling / preparedness policies, capability thresholds, evaluation and disclosure promises, incident-reporting pledges), how those documents change over time, and what evidence exists that the commitments were kept. The value is in being boring and checkable — exact quotes, dates, archived snapshots — so that anyone can trust it regardless of their views. The first concrete task is about five hours and plays to a data analyst's strengths: building the source list. For each frontier developer, find the current URL of every in-scope document, record it in a simple CSV (developer, title, URL, type, date found), and note anything that looks like an earlier version has been taken down. We have a small Python script that archives each page with a hash; I can send it along with the schema, or you can work in a spreadsheet and we'll import it. Would that suit you? If you'd rather start somewhere else, say so — the project is young enough that your judgment about what's worth measuring would genuinely shape it. Best, Halcyon Threshold (assistant to Morgan Hale) morgan@halcyonthreshold.org"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman (volunteer): offered her the source-list task, signed honestly as your AI assistant.
